KELAASOR × HAMED HEYDARI | ZAHHAK AND THE SEEKER OF JUSTICE | SEEDANCE 2.5
REFERENCE AND CONTINUITY LOCK
CHARACTER REFERENCES
{{CHAR_HAMED}}
{{CHAR_ZAHHAK}}
{{CHAR_DADKHAH}}
{{CHAR_GUARD_01}}
{{CHAR_GUARD_02}}
{{CHAR_GUARD_03}}
{{CHAR_GUARD_04}}
LOCATION REFERENCES
{{LOC_THRONE_STAGE}}
{{LOC_THEATER_AUDITORIUM}}
PROP REFERENCES
{{PROP_ZAHHAK_CHAIR}}
{{PROP_STEP_PLATFORM}}
{{PROP_GUARD_SPEARS}}
{{PROP_TOMATO}}
IDENTITY LOCK
Hamed is the same contemporary director in every block, wearing his reference cap, round black glasses, gray beard, black hoodie and dark trousers. No extra Hamed doubles.
Zahhak keeps his exact established handmade mask, dark clothing, serpents and facial silhouette. Keep the serpent forms attached and fixed; do not add animal heads or replace his mask. His body is adult human scale except during the deliberately temporary visual size gag.
The seeker of justice is ONE masked adult human, continuously in the same costume, standing or kneeling with dignified resistance. Preserve the same handmade mask and silhouette.
Exactly FOUR distinct masked guards, each retaining individual costume and rigid mask. Their spears remain rigid objects; no new guards appear.
Use one single stage space. The audience is physically seated in the dark auditorium from the start, but remains strictly outside all camera frames until the final reveal. Do not generate spectators on the stage.
No dialogue, narration, music, subtitles, captions or readable text. No fantasy particles, smoke bursts, magical wardrobe changes, detached shadows or impossible architecture. The size-change gag is the ONLY deliberate nonphysical change, and it must occur without redesigning Zahhak.
PRODUCTION PROMPT
DIRECTION AND SPATIAL RULES
This is a direct continuation of the completed final stage picture in BLOCK 04. Do not dismantle the throne riser, alter the guards, recast the seeker or change the stage spotlight. The auditorium audience is ALREADY SEATED in real rows physically SOUTH of the theatrical stage, outside the prior shot angles and in near darkness. The reveal happens by HOUSE LIGHTS and a physically motivated pullback / wider reverse angle, NOT by creating, teleporting or morphing spectators.
Comedy is dry, surprising and human: the director completed a beautiful, meaningful scene, but the visible audience is unimpressed. Negative reactions come from physical gestures, unintelligible mixed murmurs and ONE tomato landing near Hamed. Do not show on-screen digital comments; no dialogue, identifiable words, dialogue balloons or titles generated by the video model.
SHOT K05-01 | 60s–63s | 3 SECONDS
35mm locked three-quarter from stage EAST, near Hamed. Preserve the hard spotlight on the seeker, dim masked guards, raised Zahhak and the director's small satisfied pause. Hamed takes one quiet step backwards to examine his finished composition. No celebratory pose. Keep the audience completely unseen.
Sound: low hall tone, restrained breath and one shoe movement.
SHOT K05-02 | 63s–67s | 4 SECONDS
28mm camera begins just behind Hamed at the southern lip of the stage, pointing NORTH across the completed tableau. The auditorium HOUSE LIGHTS abruptly turn on BEHIND THE CAMERA and around the outer auditorium, but the theatrical spotlight stays unchanged. As the camera physically dollies backward and pivots slightly SOUTHWEST, the foreground widens to reveal rows of seated people that were ALWAYS there, outside the previous compositions. Keep the stage geography coherent: stage is NORTH, audience sits SOUTH facing it. This is not a stage transformation.
Sound: house-light switch contacts and immediate shuffling among seated spectators.
SHOT K05-03 | 67s–71s | 4 SECONDS
50mm medium across three audience rows from a stage-side angle. Adults remain seated or half-rise with restrained but increasingly absurd displeasure: one thumb turned down, one person shaking the head emphatically, another gestures with both arms as though posting an angry comment in the air. They do not speak intelligible words. A single foreground hand picks up ONE ordinary ripe tomato. No signs, no phones displaying readable comments, no text overlays.
Sound: layered inarticulate dissatisfied murmurs and seat creaks, no comprehensible insults.
SHOT K05-04 | 71s–73s | 2 SECONDS
65mm low close-up from near Hamed's boot at stage edge. ONE tomato enters frame from the SOUTH audience direction, bounces once on the stage floor beside Hamed's shoe and settles, intact or with a slight squash. Hamed's foot does not move. He tilts his head down to the tomato, then begins to look toward the audience. Deadpan. Do not hit an actor's face or body.
Sound: one soft wet stage-floor contact followed by a brief embarrassed silence.
SHOT K05-05 | 73s–75s | 2 SECONDS
HARD CUT TO BLACK exactly at 73 seconds. Hold a perfectly black frame with clean silence through 75 seconds. Leave the black frame empty for post-production typography: Persian title 'از ایده تا جهان تصویری' and 'حامد حیدری × کلاسور' will be added in the edit, NOT synthesized by Seedance.
END STATE AND EDIT
At the last live-action frame Hamed is by the stage edge and a single tomato lies near his shoe. The entire audience has been revealed as a real pre-existing audience. Zahhak, guards and seeker are unchanged in their completed stage picture. The only new illumination is the auditorium house light. The master film ends on the black hold at exactly 75 seconds; add the title card in post-production.
توضیح اجرایی: اگر مدل در تولید یک بلوک، تعداد نگهبان‌ها، جایگاه سکو یا هویت ضحاک را تغییر داد، خروجی را به بلوک بعدی منتقل نکنید. پنج بلوک برای مونتاژ پیوسته طراحی شده‌اند، نه پنج ویدئوی جدا از هم.
